Put a space inside each word.
Leave one space between the words.

items.prompt: How many spaces should separate the three words in “I can run”?

items.prompt: How many separate sounds are in the spoken word “cat”?

items.rationale: Segmenting “pen” gives three sounds: /p/, /e/, and /n/, in that order.

items.prompt: Which punctuation mark should end this statement: "The sun is bright"

items.prompt: Which word tells the color of a ripe banana?

items.rationale: “The” is used when a particular noun is clearly identified, as the moon is here.

items.prompt: Which sentence shows the events in the correct time order?

I will tie my shoes before I played. I play now. I read later.
I tied my shoes before I play. I will play now. I read later.
I tied my shoes before I played. I will play now. I read later.
items.answer: I tied my shoes before I played. I play now. I will read later.
items.rationale: The events move from the past (“tied,” “played”) to the present (“play”) and then to the future (“will read”).

items.prompt: Which word is the name of a day of the week?

items.prompt: Which word is the name of a month?

items.rationale: Autumn is a season; Tuesday is a day, and July and March are months.

items.rationale: A grocery store is a place in town where people buy food and groceries.

items.prompt: A person whose job is to deliver mail is a ____.
items.rationale: A mail carrier delivers mail to homes and businesses.

items.prompt: Mia is talking to you about her new book. What should you do while she is speaking?
choices: Ask another friend to answer for you.
Listen quietly until Mia finishes talking.
Talk over Mia so she knows you are interested.
Change the subject before Mia finishes talking.
items.answer: Listen quietly until Mia finishes talking.
items.rationale: Listening quietly and waiting for Mia to finish shows respect and does not interrupt her.

items.prompt: You want to add an idea during a group talk, but two classmates are still talking. What should you do?
choices: Talk louder so they hear your idea.
Wait for a finished speaker and your turn.
Tell them to stop talking at once.
Share your idea with only your partner.
items.answer: Wait for a finished speaker and your turn.
items.rationale: Waiting until the other speakers finish and it is your turn follows the rule for taking turns.

items.prompt: Your classmate is sharing a story, but you have a different idea. What can you do so you listen without interrupting?
choices: Change the subject so the story stops.
Start a louder conversation beside the speaker.
Wait for your turn, then share your idea.
Say your idea over the speaker’s story.
items.answer: Wait for your turn, then share your idea.
items.rationale: Waiting for your turn lets you listen to the whole story and then share your idea appropriately.

items.prompt: A full date includes a month, day, and year. Where should the comma go?
choices: After the month and before the day
After the day and before the year
After the year and before the day
Between every part of the date
items.answer: After the day and before the year
items.rationale: In a full month-day-year date, the comma separates the day from the year.

items.prompt: Which sentence correctly separates all four items in the list with commas?
choices: We packed a hat gloves, a scarf, and a coat.
We packed a hat, gloves, a scarf and, a coat.
We packed a hat, gloves, a scarf, and a coat.
We packed a hat, gloves, a scarf, and, a coat.
items.answer: We packed a hat, gloves, a scarf, and a coat.
items.rationale: Commas separate the items in the list, including a comma before the final item.

items.prompt: The race is on May 7 2026. Which choice shows that sentence with correct date punctuation?
items.rationale: The comma goes between the day and the year in a full date.

items.prompt: Which punctuation mark is missing before “and” in “We need paper, glue, scissors and tape”?
items.rationale: A comma separates the final item in a list from the other items.

items.prompt: Which pair completes the sentence? “___ am ready, and ___ are staying.”
items.rationale: “I” names the person speaking, and “they” names a group of people. Both are personal pronouns used as subjects.

items.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? “The teacher gave ___ a new book to read.”
items.rationale: “Me” is a personal pronoun used as the object of the verb “gave.”

items.prompt: Which pair completes the sentence? “This is ___ ball, and those are ___ balls.”
items.rationale: “My” shows possession of the ball being pointed out, and “their” shows possession of the other balls.

items.prompt: Which indefinite pronoun means any person, without naming one person?
items.rationale: “Anyone” means any one person. “Everyone” means all people, while the other choices do not mean a person.

items.prompt: Which sentence tells when the rain fell?
choices: The rain fell during the storm.
The rain fell toward the storm.
The rain fell beyond the storm.
The rain fell on the storm.
items.answer: The rain fell during the storm.
items.rationale: “During” tells when something happened, so “during the storm” correctly describes when the rain fell.

items.prompt: The ball rolled past the bench and stopped on the other side. The ball rolled ___ the bench.
items.rationale: “Beyond” means farther than or past something, so the ball rolled beyond the bench.

items.prompt: What time does the game start? The game starts ___ three o'clock.
items.rationale: The preposition “at” is used with a specific clock time: “at three o’clock.”

items.prompt: Which paragraph best states an opinion about recess, gives one reason, and has a closing sentence?
choices: I like recess because I can play with my friends. Recess is my favorite part of the school day.
Recess is fun. I like the swings. I go outside every day. School is a good place.
I think recess is boring because we line up a lot. I think recess is boring. It takes too much time.
My friends like recess. The swings are outside. We play at recess. The bell rings every day.
items.answer: I like recess because I can play with my friends. Recess is my favorite part of the school day.
items.rationale: The correct choice clearly states an opinion, gives the reason that the writer can play with friends, and ends with a closing sentence.

items.prompt: A writer says, “I think the library is a good place to read. The books there are quiet and interesting.” Which sentence best closes the paragraph?
choices: Reading in the library makes me feel calm and happy.
The library has many different kinds of books.
Do you like to read books at the library?
I went to the library with Sam yesterday.
items.answer: Reading in the library makes me feel calm and happy.
items.rationale: The correct choice is a concluding sentence that restates the writer’s positive opinion and ends the paragraph.

items.prompt: Which sentence gives one clear reason for the opinion “I think our class should have a class pet”?
choices: A class pet would help me learn how to care for another living thing.
I really want a class pet, and I hope we can get one soon.
There is a small hamster at my cousin’s house near school.
Do you think a class pet would be a fun choice for our room?
items.answer: A class pet would help me learn how to care for another living thing.
items.rationale: The correct choice explains why the writer thinks the class should have a pet, while the other choices do not give a clear reason.

items.prompt: A student wrote: “I think soccer is fun. I like running and kicking the ball. I like soccer because it is fun.” What should the student change?
choices: Replace the last sentence with “For me, soccer is the most fun sport of all.”
Replace the first sentence with “Soccer has many players who are on different teams.”
Keep the last sentence, and add one more fact about the school field.
Change “I like soccer” to “You like soccer,” and leave the rest as it is.
items.answer: Replace the last sentence with “For me, soccer is the most fun sport of all.”
items.rationale: The last sentence repeats the opinion instead of closing the paragraph. Replacing it with the correct choice creates a clear closing sentence.

items.prompt: Three things happened to Ben: he ate breakfast, brushed his teeth, and went to school. Which choice tells the events in the order they usually happen?
choices: First, he brushed his teeth. Then, he ate breakfast. After that, he went to school.
First, he ate breakfast. Then, he brushed his teeth. After that, he went to school.
First, he went to school. Then, he ate breakfast. After that, he brushed his teeth.
First, he ate breakfast. Then, he went to school. After that, he brushed his teeth.
items.answer: First, he ate breakfast. Then, he brushed his teeth. After that, he went to school.
items.rationale: Ben would eat breakfast, brush his teeth, and then go to school, so choice B uses the time words in the correct order.

items.prompt: Jo watched the seeds grow. He ___ the small plant in a pot. Which word shows that one event happened later?
items.rationale: “Then” connects two events and shows that the second event happened after the first.

items.prompt: A storm ended, and the sun appeared later. Which choice retells the events in the correct order?
choices: First, the storm ended. Then, the sun appeared.
First, the sun appeared. Then, the storm ended.
After the storm ended, while the sun appeared.
When the storm ended, because the sun appeared.
items.answer: First, the storm ended. Then, the sun appeared.
items.rationale: Choice A shows that the storm ended first and the sun appeared afterward.

items.prompt: Which sentence names the topic of a piece about rabbits?
choices: I hope you like my writing.
items.rationale: “I will write about rabbits” clearly names the topic, while the other choices give a fact or a closing.

items.prompt: Which choice gives a fact about the topic “rain”?
items.rationale: “Rain falls from clouds” gives a true fact about rain, while the other choices name a topic, share a feeling, or close a piece.

items.prompt: Which sentence best closes a piece about bees?
choices: Thank you for reading about bees.
items.answer: Thank you for reading about bees.
items.rationale: “Thank you for reading about bees” is a friendly closing. The other choices name the topic or give facts about bees.

items.prompt: A writer is making a short piece about dogs. Which order follows the needed parts?
choices: Name the topic, give facts, and close the piece.
Give facts, name the topic, and close the piece.
Name the topic, close the piece, and give facts.
Close the piece, give facts, and name the topic.
items.answer: Name the topic, give facts, and close the piece.
items.rationale: A complete piece should first name its topic, then give facts about it, and finally end with a closing.

items.prompt: Which action best shows a child using a computer to write a short piece with help?
choices: Type a few sentences while an adult helps.
Watch an adult type a few sentences.
Draw a picture while an adult helps.
Listen to a story while an adult helps.
items.answer: Type a few sentences while an adult helps.
items.rationale: Typing sentences on a keyboard creates a written digital piece while allowing an adult to provide support.

items.prompt: A child wants to put their own words into a tablet app. What should the child do with an adult nearby?

Draw each word with one finger.
Type each word on the on-screen keyboard.
Watch an adult type the story.
items.answer: Type each word on the on-screen keyboard.
items.rationale: Using the on-screen keyboard lets the child enter their own words into the digital writing app.

items.prompt: A key on the on-screen keyboard will not work. What should the child do?
items.rationale: Asking an adult for help allows the child to continue writing without losing the typed work.

items.prompt: A child has finished a typed story. What should the child do next with an adult's help to share the story?
choices: Tap the button that turns the tablet off.
Tap the button that sends the story.
Tap the button that opens another app.
Tap the button that erases the story.
items.answer: Tap the button that sends the story.
items.rationale: The send button publishes or shares the completed digital story with the chosen audience.

items.prompt: Nia says, “I like drawing animals.” Which reply builds on her comment and asks a question to learn more?

Drawing animals can take a long time to learn.
items.answer: That sounds fun. What animal do you like drawing most?

items.prompt: Sam says, “The book was funny.” Which response best shows you are listening and asks a question to understand more?

You should choose a different book to read next time.
items.answer: That sounds funny. What part of the book made you laugh?
items.rationale: This reply builds on Sam's comment about the funny book and asks which part made him laugh.

items.prompt: Leo says, “My grandma makes pancakes.” Which reply responds to what he said and asks another question?

Your grandma should save some pancakes for me.
items.answer: That sounds yummy. What kind of pancakes does she make?
items.rationale: This reply responds to Leo's comment and asks about the kind of pancakes his grandma makes.

items.prompt: Ana says, “We have a new puppy.” Which reply builds on her comment and asks a question to learn more?
choices: That sounds exciting. What is your new puppy like?
Do you have any other pets at your home?
I think puppies are noisy and take lots of space.
You should get a different pet that is easy to care for.
items.answer: That sounds exciting. What is your new puppy like?
items.rationale: This reply shows interest in the new puppy and asks Ana to describe what it is like.

items.prompt: Which choice explains how to wash your hands in the correct order?

Wet your hands; dry them; use soap; rub them; rinse them.
Use soap; wet your hands; dry them; rub them; rinse them.
Wet your hands; use soap; dry them; rub them; rinse them.
items.answer: Wet your hands; use soap; rub them; rinse them; dry them.
items.rationale: This choice gives the proper order: wet, soap, rub, rinse, and dry.

items.prompt: A teacher says, “Touch your nose, then clap.” Which response repeats both directions in the same order?
items.rationale: This choice correctly repeats touching the nose before clapping.

items.prompt: You want to make a peanut-butter sandwich. Which choice gives directions in the correct order?
choices: Get two bread slices; place one on top; spread peanut butter on one.
Spread peanut butter on a slice; get two bread slices; place one on top.
Get two bread slices; spread peanut butter on one; place the other on top.
Get two bread slices; spread peanut butter on both; place one on top.
items.answer: Get two bread slices; spread peanut butter on one; place the other on top.
items.rationale: This choice gets the bread, spreads peanut butter on one slice, and then places the other slice on top.

items.prompt: A teacher says, “Point to the book, then the window, then your desk.” Which choice restates the directions in the correct order?
items.rationale: This choice matches the teacher’s order: book, window, and desk.

items.prompt: Your class group is making a poster about cats. What is the best first step for finding facts?
choices: Choose a source and look for facts about cats.
Draw the poster before finding any facts.
Write what you know without checking a source.
Ask only one friend what cats are like.
items.answer: Choose a source and look for facts about cats.
items.rationale: Finding facts in a suitable source is the best first step for a group project.

items.prompt: Which research card shows the best way to collect a fact for the group's project?
choices: Cats sleep for many hours. — Animal Book
Cats are the best pets. — My opinion
I saw a cat near school. — Maybe
items.answer: Cats sleep for many hours. — Animal Book
items.rationale: The card gives a fact and names the source where the information came from.

items.prompt: Your group needs facts about bees for a shared report. Which source would be most useful?
choices: A book of made-up animal stories
items.rationale: A nonfiction book about animals is likely to provide factual information about bees.

items.prompt: Mia wrote, "The dog ran." Her partner asked, "Tell where the dog ran." Which sentence adds the detail her partner asked for?
choices: The dog ran after the ball.
The dog ran to the park.
The dog ran with a friend.
items.answer: The dog ran to the park.
items.rationale: It tells where the dog ran, directly answering the partner’s request to add a place.

items.prompt: Noah’s partner said, "Show how the character felt." Which detail should Noah add to his story?
choices: The character opened the blue door.
The character walked into the room.
The character saw a bright light.
The character smiled and felt happy.
items.answer: The character smiled and felt happy.
items.rationale: It shows how the character felt, while the other choices show actions or sights instead.

items.prompt: A writer misspelled the name of the place a bunny ran toward. Which sentence spells that place correctly?
choices: The bunny had ran to the garden.
The bunny ran to the garden.
The bunny ran to the gardeon.
The bunny ran too the garden.
items.answer: The bunny ran to the garden.
items.rationale: It spells "garden" correctly and keeps "ran" and "to" correct.

items.prompt: Anna is making a sandwich. Which choice gives a useful detail about what Anna does?
choices: Anna spreads peanut butter on bread.
items.answer: Anna spreads peanut butter on bread.
items.rationale: This sentence gives a clear detail about Anna’s action in a complete sentence. The other choices are unrelated or incomplete.

items.prompt: Jake is visiting the zoo. Which choice gives a relevant detail about the place he is visiting?
items.rationale: Watching monkeys at the zoo is a relevant detail about Jake’s visit. The other choices are unrelated or incomplete.

items.prompt: The sky is dark, and rain begins to fall during a picnic. Which choice gives a useful detail about what the family does next in a complete sentence?
choices: They continue building a tall sandcastle.
They cover the food to keep it dry.
The ocean waves crash onto the shore.
Their picnic basket is woven from wicker.
items.answer: They cover the food to keep it dry.
items.rationale: Covering the food is a relevant detail because it helps keep the food dry during the rain.

items.prompt: Ana’s blue balloon flies up above the park. Which choice gives the most likely reason it flew away?
choices: The balloon was bright blue and shiny.
Her brother held a second balloon.
The string came loose from her hand.
The park was near the river.
items.answer: The string came loose from her hand.
items.rationale: The string coming loose explains why the balloon flew away and is more relevant than the other details.
